title: When we find something, and what may leave
desc: Placeholders versus blocking, the interactive pre-flight, tool blocking and EU-only models.
learningGoal: After this lesson you can set the action and the outbound rules so the right people are interrupted at the right moment, and say exactly what may cross your organisation's boundary.

steps.title: We found something. Now what?
steps.bodyMd:
The detector has just found a customer's e-mail address in a message on its way to the AI. What should Bee Flow do with it? You answer that once, on step 3, **When we find something**, and your answer holds for everyone in the organisation.

That step opens one screen with two cards side by side, in the order they run. The first, **On every message**, asks *When we find personal data*, and there are exactly two answers:

- **Replace with placeholders** — details are swapped for labels such as `[email_1]` before the message goes to the AI. The model never sees the real values, and Bee Flow puts them back in the answer.
- **Do not send the message** — the message is stopped before it reaches the AI, and the person is asked to rewrite it without the personal data.

At Van Dijk Groep, procurement pastes supplier quotations to compare them, and placeholders keep that comparison readable. HR's re-integration dossiers are a different matter: there, stopping the message is the honest choice.

steps.question: Van Dijk Groep is on a plan that does not include placeholders. The admin opens When we find something to select Replace with placeholders. What do they find?

choices.label: It is shown, but disabled, with an Enterprise badge — so the only action they can actually save is "Do not send the message".
The card is hidden entirely on a plan without the feature, so the tab offers only one option to choose from.
choices.feedback: Both options are always shown on purpose. Hiding one once left organisations whose stored action was placeholders looking at a card with nothing selected and no explanation of why.

choices.label: The card can be selected and saved, and placeholders then work exactly as they do on any other plan.
choices.feedback: The option is disabled on a plan without the feature, so it cannot be picked there. And even where placeholders are already stored from an earlier plan, the runtime stops the message instead of replacing anything — the card shows an amber note saying exactly that.

choices.label: The whole When we find something step is locked until the plan is upgraded, so nothing on it can be saved.
choices.feedback: Only the placeholders card is gated. Blocking, the knowledge-base check and "Also protect automations" are available on every plan.

steps.explanation: Placeholders are a licensed feature and the gate sits on the option itself: disabled, badged Enterprise, with "Replacing with placeholders is an Enterprise feature." beneath it. If an organisation already had placeholders stored, the option stays visible with an amber note instead of silently deselecting itself — and Overview lists "Placeholders are not in your plan": "Your plan does not include placeholders, so these messages are stopped instead."

steps.title: A second check, right at the border
steps.bodyMd:
The action you just chose is the always-on gate: it runs on every message, silently.

The second card on the same screen, **Before it leaves your organisation** — step 4, **Leaving your org** — adds something different: **"One last check before an outside AI"**. It is a *second*, interactive check that fires just before a message goes to a model running outside your organisation, and it is the only step where people decide.

Keep the two apart. Setting the first one to "Do not send the message" and then waiting for a dialog to appear will never work: only the last check talks to people. This is the control Van Dijk Groep's sales team will actually meet, because they draft proposals on an outside model.

steps.title: Ask, hide, or do not send
steps.bodyMd:
Switch the pre-flight on and three mode cards appear. Pick one:

- **Ask** — show what was found and let the person choose: hide it, send anyway, or cancel.
- **Hide it** — hide what was found and send. Nobody is interrupted.
- **Do not send** — stop the message and ask the person to take the personal data out first.

Underneath sits **"Always show this check, even when nothing is found"**. Detection is never perfect; with this on, people also see the messages nothing was found in, and can mark a value the check missed by selecting it in the dialog.

Van Dijk Groep starts on Ask: the sales team gets to see what the shield sees before anyone trusts it to decide alone.

steps.title: What your colleague actually sees
steps.bodyMd:
In Ask mode the person does not get a refusal. They get a dialog headed **"Check this before it goes to the AI"**, with the buttons `Block`, `Send anyway` and `Redact and send` — that last one reads `Send` when there is nothing marked to hide.

Silence is not consent. While the dialog is open it waits for an answer; if the question goes unanswered for ten minutes with no dialog keeping it open — the tab was closed, say — the message is treated as blocked.

Tell your people about this before you switch it on. A dialog nobody was expecting gets clicked away, and `Send anyway` is right there.

steps.question: A Van Dijk Groep engineer chats with the self-hosted model on the company network, pastes a customer's name and e-mail, and no dialog appears — even though the pre-flight is on and set to Ask. Why?

choices.label: The pre-flight only runs for models outside your organisation, and one on your own private network counts as internal — so it is skipped.
The pre-flight only runs on the first message of a conversation, and this was not the first one.
choices.feedback: There is no such rule — later messages are checked too. A person can tick "Remember my choice for this conversation" in the dialog to stop being asked again, but that is their decision, not a first-message rule.

choices.label: Ask mode only fires for attached files and documents, never for text that somebody types.
choices.feedback: Ask mode applies to a typed message as much as to an attachment — the dialog even has its own attachment wording.

choices.label: A model at an address the shield does not recognise is always treated as internal.
choices.feedback: The opposite is true: an unrecognised provider or address is treated as external, so the check runs. Only explicit self-hosted types and private, loopback or .local addresses count as internal.

steps.explanation: The last check's scope is "external" — it exists to catch data crossing your boundary. Self-hosted runtimes and addresses on a private network stay inside, so nothing is checked and nobody is interrupted. Anything unknown is treated as external on purpose, so a misconfigured endpoint fails towards checking rather than away from it. The always-on gate under When we find something still applies either way.

steps.title: Holding data back from tools
steps.bodyMd:
A chat is not the only way out. Tools are the things the AI can use for you — search the web, open a file, send an e-mail — and the shield lets you name the kinds of personal data a tool may never carry.

That is not on this screen but in the table on **What we look for**, as two columns beside *Hide from AI*:

- **Hold back · outside tools** — tools that send data outside your organisation, such as a connected app or a search engine. Enterprise.
- **Hold back · own server** — tools that stay on your own server, on every plan.

The checks screen points there itself: *Tool calls skip ① and ②. They follow the tool columns in the matrix.* If a held-back kind turns up in the arguments, the call is refused before it is made, and the AI is told to continue without that information or to ask the person how to proceed. Anything that does come back has that data stripped out, and the refusal is recorded.

steps.title: Search boxes and where the model lives
steps.bodyMd:
Three more switches sit on the **Before it leaves your organisation** card, each aimed at a specific leak:

- **Protect web searches** — stop search terms that contain personal data from reaching an outside search engine. Enterprise.
- **No web search while a file is attached** — so nothing from an attached document ends up in a search box.
- **Use only AI hosted in the EU** — chats only go to AI models hosted in the EU, set up under AI Config → Chat Models. It covers models only; connected apps such as Gmail follow the tool columns.

The two search switches only appear once a search provider is configured, and the EU switch only once EU-hosted models exist.

For Van Dijk Groep, a supplier's company name in a search box is fine. A named contact person is not.

steps.title: Which control does this?
steps.instruction: Van Dijk Groep's management wrote down five rules. Match each rule to the Privacy Shield control that actually implements it.

pairs.left: Names must never reach an outside model, but nobody at Van Dijk Groep should be interrupted about it.
pairs.note: Hide it redacts what was found and sends the message without a dialog. Ask is the mode that puts the decision in front of the person.

pairs.left: For the first month a person must lay eyes on every outbound message, not only the ones with a hit.
pairs.right: Always show this check, even when nothing is found
pairs.note: Ask alone only pauses on a hit. This checkbox is what surfaces clean messages so a missed value can still be marked.

pairs.left: A connected app must never be able to carry a citizen service number out of the building.
pairs.right: The Hold back · outside tools column on What we look for
pairs.note: The call is refused before dispatch when a listed category appears in its arguments.

pairs.left: Quotes from an attached dossier must not end up in a search engine's query box.
pairs.right: No web search while a file is attached
pairs.note: With a document attached, web search is switched off for the conversation, so nothing from the file can be typed into a search.

pairs.left: Our data protection officer signs off only if answers are generated on European infrastructure.
pairs.right: Use only AI hosted in the EU
pairs.note: Chats are routed to the EU models configured under AI Config → Chat Models; the card only appears once those exist.

steps.title: Your turn: write the outbound policy
steps.instruction: Van Dijk Groep's sales team wants to draft proposals on a strong model that runs outside the organisation, working from a customer export full of names, e-mail addresses and phone numbers. For the first month the admin wants a human eye on every outbound message; after that, no interruptions. Write the settings you would save, in plain sentences: which mode for "One last check before an outside AI" in month one and which afterwards, whether you tick "Always show this check, even when nothing is found", and one tool or search control you would switch on as well. Say why for each.
steps.placeholder: e.g. Month one: pre-flight on, mode Ask, and tick "Always show this check, even when nothing is found" so the team also sees clean messages and can mark what the detector missed. From month two I switch to ... because ...

steps.title: The unattended paths
steps.bodyMd:
Two settings on the **On every message** card cover the places where nobody is watching, and both are on unless you switch them off.

**Also protect automations** checks the data and the AI steps of automations the same way as chat. Van Dijk Groep's Monday-morning report builds itself at five in the morning, with nobody at the keyboard — exactly where an interactive Ask would help nobody — so the always-on action carries the weight there.

**Also check knowledge bases when documents are added** replaces personal data before a document is stored, not when it is read. That matters twice over: a knowledge base quotes its documents to people who never saw the original file, and the check cannot be undone afterwards. The stored text is the checked text.

steps.title: Switch the pre-flight on — we will verify it
steps.instruction: Open the Privacy Shield. If "Protect personal data" is off under Overview, switch it on first — the numbered steps stay inactive until it is. Then, on Leaving your org, switch on "One last check before an outside AI", pick a mode (start with Ask), press Save changes and wait for "Saved successfully!". Now prove it: send a chat message containing a name and an e-mail address on a model that runs outside your organisation, and watch for the dialog "Check this before it goes to the AI".

steps.title: What you can do now
steps.bodyMd:
- **Choose the action** under When we find something. Placeholders keep a message usable; "Do not send the message" keeps it inside. Placeholders are a licensed feature — without it, those messages are stopped instead.
- **Set the last check** under Leaving your org to Ask, Hide it or Do not send, and add "Always show this check, even when nothing is found" when you want a human eye on everything. It skips models running on your own network.
- **Name what may not cross the boundary**: kinds held back in the tool columns on What we look for, protected web searches, no search while a file is attached, and EU-hosted models only.

All of it can be changed back — but text already stored in a knowledge base stays as it was checked.

Next chapter: the evidence that these settings fired.

ex-shield-org-outbound-policy.title: An outbound policy for the sales team
ex-shield-org-outbound-policy.task: Write the outbound settings for Van Dijk Groep's sales team: which mode for "One last check before an outside AI" for the first month and which afterwards, whether to tick "Always show this check, even when nothing is found", and at least one tool or search control to switch on — with a reason for each choice.
criteria: Names Ask (with a human in the loop) for the first month and a less interruptive mode — Hide it, or a reasoned case for staying on Ask — afterwards, with a stated reason for the change.
Decides explicitly on "Always show this check, even when nothing is found" and explains what it buys: clean messages are also shown, so a value the detector missed can still be marked.

Adds at least one real control — the Hold back · outside tools column on What we look for, Protect web searches, No web search while a file is attached, or Use only AI hosted in the EU — correctly described.
Shows awareness that the last check only fires for models outside the organisation, or that the always-on action under When we find something still applies underneath.
ex-shield-org-outbound-policy.guidance: Do not pass an answer that only repeats the three mode names without choosing, that invents settings which do not exist (per-team or per-user modes, a per-message approval queue), that claims the last check also covers a self-hosted model, or that confuses the last check with the action under When we find something. A short answer is fine if it makes the three decisions concretely and gives a reason for each.

practiceTopic.title: Shield: the action and the outbound rules
practiceTopic.summary: How an organisation decides what happens to personal data it finds, and what may cross its boundary.
facts: Step 3, When we find something, offers two actions on the card On every message: "Replace with placeholders" (labels such as [email_1], restored in the answer, an Enterprise feature) and "Do not send the message".
"One last check before an outside AI", on the card Before it leaves your organisation (step 4, Leaving your org), is a second, interactive check with three modes: Ask, Hide it, and Do not send.
The last check only fires for providers outside the organisation; a self-hosted model on a private network is treated as internal and skipped, while an unrecognised provider is treated as external.
"Always show this check, even when nothing is found" also pauses on clean messages, so a person can mark something the detector missed.

In Ask mode the person sees the dialog "Check this before it goes to the AI" with Block, Send anyway and Redact and send; an open dialog waits, and a decision left unanswered for ten minutes is treated as blocked.
Tools are governed by the Hold back · outside tools (Enterprise) and Hold back · own server columns on What we look for; a tool call carrying a held-back kind is refused before it is made.
"No web search while a file is attached" and "Use only AI hosted in the EU" are separate switches on the same card; the EU switch only appears once EU chat models are configured.
"Also protect automations" and "Also check knowledge bases when documents are added" are both on by default, and the knowledge-base check applies before a document is stored and cannot be undone.

actionChecks.label: Turn on the check before an outside AI
actionChecks.hint: In Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield → Leaving your org, switch on "One last check before an outside AI", pick a mode, and press Save changes.

endpoints.returns: { orgId, summary: { shieldEnabled, dlpEnabled, ... }, rawShape, resolved: { enabled, dlpEnabled, dlpMode, dlpScope, ... } } — the configuration the runtime actually honours. requireAuth + org membership only (no org_admin), and :org is substituted with the learner's own organisation. NOTE: resolved.dlpMode falls back to 'ask' whenever nothing is stored, so it can never prove that a mode was chosen — it is not verified.

criteria.label: The shield itself is switched on
criteria.hint: On the Overview tab, "Protect personal data" must be on — the numbered steps stay inactive until it is.
criteria.rule: GET /api/org-privacy-shield/:org/effective → summary.shieldEnabled is true (it is false whenever the org shield resolves to nothing).

criteria.label: The outbound check is switched on and saved
criteria.hint: Leaving your org → "One last check before an outside AI", pick a mode, then Save changes and wait for "Saved successfully!".
criteria.rule: GET /api/org-privacy-shield/:org/effective → resolved.dlpEnabled === true, i.e. the saved org config the runtime reads, not the unsaved form state.
